newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand's Amnuay confirms he will resign.
newsitem.headline: Thailand's Amnuay confirms he will resign.

text.p: Thailand's Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan confirmed on Thursday that he planned to resign from his post, but said he had not met the prime minister on the matter yet.
"I had long planned to resign but I had to hang on until my duty to welcome the visiting Singapore prime minister was over," the minister told reporters.
The embattled minister is expected to submit his resignation letter to Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh sometime today, his aides said.

"I will not change my mind (about the resignation)," said Amnuay when asked if he would reconsider his intention to resign. He was speaking at the Government House where the prime minister's office is located.
Amnuay's imminent resignation follows conflict between him and his political rivals in Chavalit's six-party coalition government over Amnuay's management of the ailing Thai economy.

Thailand is faced with a severe economic downturn, the worst in more than a decade, and its finance and property sectors are in major trouble. Consumer spending has slowed, interest rates remain high, affecting businesses, and the baht has been the target of speculative attacks.
This week Amnuay lost a battle with some of his ministerial colleagues to increase excise taxes on some consumer goods when the cabinet reversed his earlier decision to raise taxes.
Amnuay had lost face after the decision was reversed, analysts said.

Political sources said some key members of Chavalit's own party, the New Aspiration Party, and the Chart Pattana Party, which is the second-largest in the administration, were behind the moves to get rid of the unelected Amnuay.
Finding a successor for Amnuay would be a tough job for the prime minister, analysts said.
They also expect Thailand's battered stock market and the baht to open sharply lower on the news.
"The stock and money markets will be greatly affected by the expected resignation of the finance minister," said Thanadech Mahapokai of Book Club Finance and Securities.
The stock market is languishing at a 98-month low after closing 14.78 points lower at 482.94 on Wednesday on rumours that Amnuay planned to resign.
In the offshore market, the baht was quoted much lower at 24.900/000 to the dollar on Thursday morning compared with 23.530/630 late on Wednesday.
